title: Curtain Wall Firestop System
jurisdiction: British Columbia code context; sample says its format follows the City of Vancouver template, but does not identify the project jurisdiction or AHJ
document_date: 2025-04 (PDF metadata creation date 2025-04-08; no issue date printed)

facts.text: The guide calls this a long-form sample alternative solution and says its format follows the City of Vancouver alternative-solution template.

The described building is a new 12-storey mixed-use office tower over a 3-level below-grade parkade, with encapsulated mass timber above grade, noncombustible below grade, the listed occupancies and fire protection systems. The guide does not name a project location.

The described prefabricated curtain wall leaves a gap up to 200 mm between the CLT floor slab edge and the curtain wall from the second to twelfth storeys. The sample cites Sentence 3.1.8.3.(4) for maintaining fire-separation continuity and proposes a custom firestop detail.

The sample compares its proposed firestop to Intertek Design No. STI/BPF 120-11 and describes 5-ply CLT at least 175 mm thick, a minimum 150 mm mineral-wool depth, at least 25% compression, 3 mm firestop spray and 12.7 mm overlap. It also describes moving curtain-wall anchors from the top of the slab to steel plates at the slab-edge mid-depth.

The guide contains an internal reference mismatch: it identifies Sentence 3.1.8.3.(4) as the applicable provision but says the listed objective/function pairs are attributed to Sentence 3.1.18.2.(1), and repeats that sentence in the table.

An accessible manufacturer-hosted listing marked 'Reproduced courtesy of Intertek Testing Services NA Ltd.' identifies Design No. STI/BPF 120-11, a 2-hour F-rating, 3/4-hour T-rating and a minimum 5-ply, 175 mm CLT floor assembly. The retrieved copy is a seven-page listing dated July 31, 2023.

limitations: This is explicitly a published sample, not an actual application or issued variance.
The project location, AHJ and sample-specific code edition are unstated; the City of Vancouver template reference does not establish the project's jurisdiction.
The guide's objective/function attribution appears internally inconsistent with its stated applicable provision; this has been flagged rather than repaired by inference.

The attached seven-page copy is hosted by the product manufacturer and says it is reproduced courtesy of Intertek. Direct retrieval of the Intertek document viewer redirected repeatedly, and web open timed out; the exact current Intertek-hosted file was not captured.
The guide's generic 12-storey project description closely resembles the preceding ceiling-finish sample; the guide does not say whether the two are the same example building.
